Typography resources

17 articles for learning typography, from vocabulary and print history to font pairing and modern web design.

Concepts and vocabulary

Start with these three articles. Use the glossary while you explore the font library.

  1. 1

    Practical Typography

    Typography in Ten Minutes

    A short introduction to font choice, text size, line spacing, and line length.

    The recommendation to buy paid fonts is the author’s preference, not a requirement for learning typography.

    https://practicaltypography.com/typography-in-ten-minutes.html
  2. 2

    Nielsen Norman Group

    Typography Terms: Glossary

    Illustrated definitions of x-height, kerning, leading, weights, families, and other typography vocabulary.

    Recommended starting point for vocabulary study.

    https://www.nngroup.com/articles/typography-terms-ux/
  3. 3

    Google Fonts Knowledge

    Making Sense of Typographic Classifications

    Understand different kinds of typefaces and use classification to narrow your choices.

    https://fonts.google.com/knowledge/introducing_type/making_sense_of_typographic_classifications

Choosing and pairing fonts

Learn how to choose type for a purpose, combine families, and evaluate readability.

  1. 4

    Google Design

    Choosing Web Fonts: A Beginner’s Guide

    Connect font selection to project needs, language coverage, available styles, readability, and intended use.

    https://design.google/library/choosing-web-fonts-beginners-guide
  2. 5

    Jonathan Z. White / freeCodeCamp

    Typography can make or break your design: a process for choosing type

    A practical font-selection workflow, from project goals to a reusable type guide.

    Published in 2017; some linked services and tool names are historical. Read the organized Choosing Type article, including resources and ideas, or practice the workflow in the Choosing Type roadmap.

    https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/typography-can-make-your-design-or-break-it-7be710aadcfe/
  3. 6

    Nielsen Norman Group

    The Dos and Don’ts of Pairing Typefaces

    Visual examples of contrast, consistency, distinct characters, and using multiple weights within one family.

    Start your pairing study here.

    https://www.nngroup.com/articles/pairing-typefaces/
  4. 7

    Google Fonts Knowledge

    Pairing Typefaces

    An introduction to selecting a secondary typeface to accompany your primary one.

    https://fonts.google.com/knowledge/choosing_type/pairing_typefaces
  5. 8

    Google Fonts Knowledge

    Pairing Typefaces Using the Font Matrix

    A deeper approach to combining typefaces based on the construction of their letterforms.

    Read after the introductory pairing articles.

    https://fonts.google.com/knowledge/choosing_type/pairing_typefaces_based_on_their_construction_using_the_font_matrix
  6. 9

    Nielsen Norman Group

    Best Font for Online Reading: No Single Answer

    Research showing why a font that works well for one reader may perform differently for another.

    Useful when evaluating claims that one font is universally best.

    https://www.nngroup.com/articles/best-font-for-online-reading/

History of print and web typography

Read these in order: print design, desktop publishing, early web constraints, and modern web fonts. This is a focused route through Western print and web history, not a complete global history of printing.

  1. 10

    Victoria and Albert Museum

    William Morris: Literature and Book Design

    Shows type, margins, spacing, illustration, and readability being designed together before the web.

    Stage 1: print design.

    https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/william-morris-text
  2. 11

    Computer History Museum

    PostScript: A Digital Printing Press

    The technology behind the desktop-publishing transformation of the 1980s.

    Stage 2: digital publishing.

    https://computerhistory.org/blog/postscript-a-digital-printing-press/
  3. 12

    W3C

    Fonts for the Web: Rationale, 1996

    A historical document explaining the case for downloadable web fonts.

    Stage 3: early web constraints. The URL reflects a later republication of the historical rationale.

    https://www.w3.org/TR/2022/NOTE-font-rationale-20220414/
  4. 13

    Jason Santa Maria / A List Apart

    On Web Typography

    A 2009 account of moving beyond system fonts, images, and Flash, with advice on selection and pairing.

    Stage 4: the web-font transition. Read technical and marketplace claims in their historical context.

    https://alistapart.com/article/on-web-typography/
  5. 14

    W3C

    WOFF 1.0: A Milestone on W3C’s Journey of Fonts on the Web

    A retrospective connecting early standards work to downloadable web-font delivery.

    Stage 5: how web fonts became established.

    https://www.w3.org/blog/2026/woff-1-0-a-milestone-on-w3cs-journey-of-fonts-on-the-web/

Typography on modern websites

Connect typography decisions to responsive layouts, CSS, and performance.

  1. 15

    web.dev

    Typography

    Responsive sizing, line length, spacing, hierarchy, and font loading.

    A bridge from typography theory to your websites.

    https://web.dev/learn/design/typography
  2. 16

    MDN Web Docs

    Variable Fonts

    Adjustable weight, width, optical size, and how variable fonts are implemented in CSS.

    https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Fonts/Variable_fonts
  3. 17

    web.dev

    Best Practices for Fonts

    Tradeoffs between system and downloaded fonts, loading delays, layout shifts, file formats, and variable fonts.

    Variable fonts do not automatically mean smaller downloads.

    https://web.dev/articles/font-best-practices

Try what you read

After each article, pick one term, find it in two fonts, change one setting, and explain what changed in your own words.
